claim: An unchecked dispatch base lets the main session exclude PR changes from the required CI gates using an ordinary command.
trigger: A feature branch contains commit C1 changing web/index.html followed by C2 changing docs/testing.md; run `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref feature -f base=<C1-SHA>`.
expected_vs_actual: CI should cover the whole PR, including browser and performance validation for web/index.html; instead selection sees only the documentation change, skips those jobs, and required accepts the same incomplete selection. Validate that the supplied base belongs to dev history before trusting it.
evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml:41 and :159 pass inputs.base to both selection and aggregation; crates/harness/src/gates.rs:230-243 accepts any resolvable comparison commit, and :299-303 recomputes against that same input. crates/harness/src/gates/tests.rs:68-70 pins documentation-only selection skipping browser. crates/harness/src/agents/role.rs:67-69 and rules/github.rs:97-105 permit workflow commands from the main session.

votes.evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml:41 and :159 trust inputs.base for selection and aggregate validation. For C1 changing web/index.html followed by C2 changing docs/testing.md, supplying C1 selects only the documentation diff: crates/harness/src/gates/paths.rs:45 computes merge-base(C1, HEAD), which is C1; gates/tests.rs:68-88 demonstrates browser skipped and aggregate accepted for that selection. agents/rules/github.rs:97-105 permits the main session's ordinary workflow command. This contradicts the task's 'same gates as a PR run'. It proves incomplete CI coverage, not a branch-protection bypass.

.github/workflows/ci.yml:41 and :159 trust inputs.base for dispatched selection and aggregation. crates/harness/src/gates/paths.rs:46 computes changes from the supplied commit's merge base with HEAD; gates.rs:302 recomputes against that same unchecked input. Supplying C1 in the stated C1-web/C2-docs sequence excludes the web change, and gates/tests.rs:71 confirms documentation-only selection skips browser validation. This establishes incomplete dispatched CI. Its scope does not extend to an eligible PR-required check: pull_request runs use the event base instead, and the workflow_dispatch checks are excluded as established by F3.

The bypass is real and duplicates F2, but the stated severity rules classify weakening a gate as critical. With web-changing C1 followed by docs-only C2, .github/workflows/ci.yml:41 selects against C1 and :159 validates against that same unchecked input. gates/paths.rs:43-57 excludes C1's changes; gates/tests.rs:40-58 establishes web/index.html requires browser/performance, while :64-88 establishes docs-only selection accepts their skips. agents/role.rs:67-69 and agents/rules/github.rs:97-105 leave the reported workflow command available to Main.

.github/workflows/ci.yml:41 and :159 trust the supplied base. crates/harness/src/gates/paths.rs:45 computes its merge base with HEAD, so supplying ancestor C1 excludes C1's changes; gates.rs:302 validates against the same narrowed comparison. However, this only produces an incomplete successful dispatch run: GitHub's documented workflow_dispatch exclusion prevents it from satisfying the PR's required check. The residual validation-scope issue is minor, not a demonstrated major merge-gate bypass.

claim: Trusting an unchecked dispatch base allows an ordinary workflow command to omit required PR gates while still passing the required aggregate.
trigger: An open PR has commit C changing crates/simulation/src/lib.rs followed by commit D changing only docs/testing.md; the main session runs `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref <PR-branch> -f base=<C-SHA>`.
expected_vs_actual: CI should select gates for the complete PR against dev, including browser and performance checks; instead it compares C to D, selects only documentation/static work, skips the other jobs, and accepts those skips in required. Validate the supplied base against the PR's merge base with dev before using it.
evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml:41 and :160 use inputs.base for both selection and aggregate validation; crates/harness/src/gates/paths.rs:43-57 compares the supplied commit with HEAD without checking dev; crates/harness/src/gates.rs:226-244 accepts that comparison and :283-290 accepts skipped unselected jobs. Existing tests at crates/harness/src/gates/tests.rs:40-58 establish simulation impact, while :64-88 establish that a docs-only selection passes with browser, performance and fuzz jobs skipped.

votes.evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml:41 and :159 trust inputs.base for selection and validation. For simulation commit C followed by docs-only D, supplying C makes crates/harness/src/gates/paths.rs:45-54 compare C with D, omitting the simulation change. crates/harness/src/gates.rs:283-290 accepts skipped unselected jobs, and gates/tests.rs:64-88 confirms the docs-only aggregate passes. This weakens gate coverage through an ordinary main-session command; agents/rules/github.rs:97-105 restricts workflow execution only for subagents. Critical gate-weakening is upheld, without claiming this dispatch satisfies merge protection.

.github/workflows/ci.yml:41 and :159 introduce the same unchecked-base defect as F1. For simulation commit C followed by documentation commit D, base=C excludes the simulation change. crates/harness/src/gates.rs:283-290 accepts skipped unselected jobs, and :302 recomputes against the same supplied base, so required can pass. gates/tests.rs:40-58 establishes simulation impact and :64-88 establishes documentation-only acceptance. The rule treats 'a test or gate weakened to pass' as critical; this ordinary command weakens the dispatched aggregate's coverage. This duplicates F1 and does not independently prove that GitHub permits merging.

.github/workflows/ci.yml:41 and :159 trust inputs.base for selection and aggregate validation. With simulation-changing C followed by docs-only D, base=C makes crates/harness/src/gates/paths.rs:43-57 compare only C..D. crates/harness/src/gates.rs:230-244 performs no dev-history validation; :283-290 accepts skipped unselected jobs. Tests at crates/harness/src/gates/tests.rs:64-88 confirm docs-only selection accepts browser/performance/fuzz skips. The unconditional preflight excludes those gates (gates/registry.json:25-34). agents/rules/github.rs:97-105 permits this ordinary command for Main. This weakens required CI and meets the stated critical severity.

.github/workflows/ci.yml:41 accepts C as the comparison base, and crates/harness/src/gates.rs:283-290 accepts skipped jobs absent from that selection. The narrowed required aggregate can therefore pass, but it is not eligible to satisfy the PR's required check, as documented for workflow_dispatch. This duplicates F1's minor validation-scope issue; the claimed critical weakening of the enforced PR gate is not established.

claim: Dispatching CI with workflow_dispatch does not provide an eligible required check for the rebased pull request.
trigger: An auto-merge PR falls behind dev, the updater rebases it with GITHUB_TOKEN, carries review, and successfully dispatches ci.yml on its head branch.
expected_vs_actual: The dispatched required job should satisfy the PR's merge requirement; GitHub excludes workflow_dispatch job checks from pull-request evaluation, so passing this run does not unblock the PR.
evidence: update.rs:259-269 dispatches CI, and .github/workflows/ci.yml:146-163 supplies required only as a workflow job. [GitHub's required-check documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/how-tos/merge-and-close-pull-requests/troubleshooting-required-status-checks#checks-from-some-workflow-jobs-are-not-evaluated) explicitly states that workflow_dispatch checks on a PR head branch are not evaluated for the PR and do not satisfy required checks in a branch ruleset.

votes.evidence: crates/harness/src/ship/postpush/update.rs:259-269 creates a workflow_dispatch on the rebased branch, and .github/workflows/ci.yml:146-163 reports required as a workflow job. GitHub's cited documentation explicitly says workflow_dispatch job checks on a PR head branch are excluded from PR evaluation and cannot satisfy required status checks in a branch ruleset. Thus a successful rebase, carry and dispatch does not provide the eligible required check promised by this flow. Major is upheld.

crates/harness/src/ship/postpush/update.rs:265 dispatches workflow_dispatch; .github/workflows/ci.yml:146 creates required solely as a workflow job. The task relies on 'the dispatched required check counting for branch protection'. GitHub's cited documentation explicitly excludes workflow_dispatch job checks from PR evaluation and required status checks in branch rulesets. A successful dispatch therefore does not establish the intended eligible check. Live protection settings were not verified.

crates/harness/src/ship/postpush/update.rs:265 dispatches ci.yml through workflow_dispatch; .github/workflows/ci.yml:146 defines required as a workflow job, with no separate publication of an eligible check. GitHub explicitly documents that workflow_dispatch job checks on a PR head do not satisfy required checks in a branch ruleset. The successful rebase-and-dispatch sequence therefore does not provide the intended eligible required check. Major.

crates/harness/src/ship/postpush/update.rs:265 dispatches ci.yml; .github/workflows/ci.yml:146 supplies required solely through a workflow job. GitHub explicitly documents that workflow_dispatch job checks are excluded from PR evaluation and cannot satisfy required checks in a branch ruleset: https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/how-tos/merge-and-close-pull-requests/troubleshooting-required-status-checks#checks-from-some-workflow-jobs-are-not-evaluated. This supports the major finding; live repository enforcement was not reproduced.
